text.p: Bonds were hitting new highs as Spain surged again on the back of positive inflation news and traders said that the peaks may not yet have been seen.

"The rise may not halt yet if the foreigners come in in greater strength," said one trader. Beside good Spanish inflation numbers, the markets were also relieved that the U.S. Federal Reserve did not lift rates at its meeting on Wednesday.
"Technically, the future is inclined upwards," added the trader. Next resistance was at 105.50, while support was drawn at 104.25.
Traders said the stance of the foreign investors could depend on reaction to this afternoon's inflation and retail sales figures from the U.S.
"After several days of consolidation around 140-145 basis points against the (German 10-year) Bund, we are moving to test an area around 135," said another trader, referring the yield gap.

Traders said that the short and medium part of the curve were also well-supported by the Federal Reserve decision because the Bank of Portugal was now seen as having ample arguments for a rate cut soon.
